title: Shah Rukh Khan Said No to Jailer 2. Hrithik Roshan Said Tell Me More.
excerpt: Bollywood's Greek God is reportedly in advanced talks for the most coveted cameo in Indian cinema — and a viral childhood video with Rajinikanth just made the internet weep.
body:
There is a seat in Indian cinema right now that every actor in the country would kill for. It belongs to **Jailer 2**, the sequel to Rajinikanth's 2023 blockbuster, and for months it had one name written on it in invisible ink: **Shah Rukh Khan**.

SRK was approached. SRK was interested. And then SRK said no.

The reason, according to multiple industry reports, is exquisitely Shah Rukh: he didn't want a single frame of his face on a screen before **King**, his December 2026 comeback vehicle directed by **Siddharth Anand**, hit theatres. With *King* marking daughter **Suhana Khan's** big-screen debut, the man who built an empire on timing decided that exclusivity was worth more than sharing screen space with the Thalaivar himself.

> "He was initially open to the idea, but the primary conflict arose from the release timelines. SRK reportedly felt that a big-screen appearance so close to his own lead release might dilute the exclusivity of his return." — Pinkvilla

So Sun Pictures, the production house behind *Jailer 2*, did what any sensible producer would do. They picked up the phone and called the only other Bollywood star who could credibly fill that seat: **Hrithik Roshan**.

## The Greek God Picks Up the Phone

According to a report by Tamil media outlet **Valai Pechu**, Hrithik is now in "advanced talks" for a pivotal cameo in the Nelson Dilipkumar-directed sequel. No official confirmation has dropped from either camp, but the industry whisper network is operating at full volume. If the deal closes, it would give *Jailer 2* the kind of pan-India star wattage that makes distributors salivate — Rajinikanth and Hrithik Roshan sharing a frame for what would essentially be the first time in their adult careers.

The already stacked cast includes **Mohanlal**, **Shiva Rajkumar**, **Mithun Chakraborty**, **Vijay Sethupathi**, **Ramya Krishnan**, and **Vidya Balan**. Adding Hrithik to that lineup isn't just casting — it's an arms race.

## A Beard, a Boy, and a Memory

What has made this story travel beyond trade circles is a vintage video that resurfaced on social media over the weekend. In it, a young Hrithik recalls working with Rajinikanth as a child artist in the 1986 film **Bhagwaan Dada** — a movie produced by his father, Rakesh Roshan.

> "This is a photograph of a very ignorant, little, foolish boy who had no idea he was standing with the greatest legend of all time. For me, he was Rajini Uncle." — Hrithik Roshan

He goes on to describe how Rajinikanth would take the blame every time young Hrithik flubbed a shot. "He would say, 'Sorry, my fault,' but it was actually my fault. This happened every single time so that I, a child, would not get conscious."

Forty years later, the boy who once held Rajinikanth's beard on a film set might just walk onto one as his equal. The internet, predictably, is in its feelings.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

*Jailer 2* has already sealed a massive streaming deal, and the film — now reportedly pushed to an October release window after reshoots — will land on OTT platforms globally. For NRIs who grew up watching both Rajinikanth and Hrithik dominate different corners of Indian cinema, the prospect of seeing them together is the kind of crossover event that doesn't come around twice.

The first *Jailer* grossed over ₹600 crore worldwide. With this cast, the sequel isn't just aiming to match that number — it's aiming to obliterate it. For the Indian diaspora, the excitement surrounding *Jailer 2* not only highlights the strong ties to their cultural roots but also has implications for remittances and the global reach of Indian cinema. As these films gain traction, they can inspire greater interest in Indian culture, leading to increased travel back home and stronger family connections.

No confirmation yet from Hrithik's team or Sun Pictures. But in Bollywood, when the whispers get this loud, the announcement is usually just a press conference away.
